faq.a: Aayesha represents Arabic عائشة (ʿĀʾishah), associated with living or alive; it is related to the Arabic root ع ي ش.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aayesha?
faq.a: The recorded form عائشة is Arabic and is well established as a feminine personal name.
Yes. The underlying Arabic form recorded here is عائشة (ʿĀʾishah).

faq.q: What is the root of Aayesha?
faq.a: The name is associated with the Arabic root ع ي ش (ʿ-y-sh), related to living or life.
Aayesha is a traditional Muslim personal name, including through the historical figure ʿĀʾishah bint Abī Bakr; the lexical meaning and historical bearer are distinct facts.
The personal name عائشة is not explicitly given as a named individual in the Qur'an; its prominence in Islamic tradition comes through other historical sources.

faq.q: What does Aayesha mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written عائشہ and commonly glossed as زندہ or جیتی جاگتی.
The supplied “aa-ye-sha” is an approximate romanization; pronunciation varies by language and transliteration.

faq.a: The record classifies Aayesha as feminine, consistent with the Arabic form; regional frequency data is not supplied.
